question: Loop diuretics such as furosemide produce their diuretic effect by inhibiting which transporter?

answers.text: NKCC2 (Na-K-2Cl cotransporter) in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Furosemide inhibits NKCC2, preventing sodium, potassium, and chloride reabsorption in the thick ascending limb, producing a large natriuretic response.

answers.text: NCC (Na-Cl cotransporter) in the distal convoluted tubule

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. NCC is the target of thiazide diuretics, not loop diuretics.

answers.text: ENaC (epithelial sodium channel) in the collecting duct

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. ENaC is blocked by amiloride, a potassium-sparing diuretic.
Incorrect. Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (e.g. acetazolamide) act in the proximal tubule; loop diuretics act in the thick ascending limb.

overallFeedback.feedback: Loop diuretics inhibit NKCC2 in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle. This site handles ~25% of filtered sodium, explaining their high potency.
Excellent. NKCC2 inhibition prevents concentration of the medullary interstitium, abolishing the driving force for water reabsorption — hence loop diuretics are the most potent diuretics available.
